question: Does the 0.4.19 tree pass on a POSIX host with 447 tests, six gates, 6/6 negative controls, the same byte account as Windows, and the two R69 unit files green?

host.kernel: Linux rjjRobert 6.6.114.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Mon Dec  1 20:46:23 UTC 2025 x86_64 GNU/Linux
host.how: WSL2; the tracked tree copied into the Linux filesystem and never run through /mnt/c; node_modules, dist and *.tsbuildinfo excluded so tsc -b could emit on this host

installed_dist_cli.what: node packages/plugin/dist/cli.js verify on this host, against the fixture set the package ships

r69_unit_files_on_posix.what: the fourteen measured/control cases for P-0053 and P-0054

governance_files_on_posix.what: the fact pack, the handoff evidence index and live claims, the patch census, and both first screens

windows_tree.what: the same tree measured on Windows before this run

not_measured.cold_directory_install: not re-run on POSIX this round: the 0.4.19 registry copy was installed on Windows (install-acceptance-2026-11-18T16-20-00.000Z.json)
not_measured.npx: not re-run this round for the same reason
not_measured.explain_sessions_on_this_host: this Linux home has no ~/.dsh/sessions, so the live findings are measured on the Windows host and by the fixtures/tests
not_measured.desktop_app: not a POSIX claim: the app is measured on Windows only

limits: one Linux host (WSL2) and one node build; this is not a distribution matrix
the suite reads files, so a POSIX pass proves the tests are portable, not that the pages are right on darwin
no resident provider ran on this host: the probe mounts the listener directly, so nothing here re-proves a repair on Linux
